_doc: #868 THE nav-shape ledger. Every app's navigation is ONE declaration in build.json::ui (bottom_nav ids min_bottom..max_bottom, 2..8, sections[].pages[] with optional pages[] one strip lower, default_section) drawn by libs:bottomnav (BottomNavIsland/BottomNavIslandView for the bar, PageTabs/PageTabsView for the pill strips) and read through NavDecl. Read by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-nav-shape-guard.py (nav-shape-guard.yml). THE BASELINE IS ALL-EXEMPT: no app has migrated yet, so every app below is exempt WITH THE REASON it is, and the guard is green today. Each migration batch removes its apps' entries in the same commit it lands, and from then on the app is held to N1-N5. Removing an entry is the only way to opt an app IN; adding one needs a reason a reviewer can disagree with.
_doc_rules: N1 ui.bottom_nav is min_bottom..max_bottom ids (2..8: the owner lifted the cap of 5 in 2026-10; the island never scrolls: a bar whose equal cells fit is drawn as always, a crowded one widens past 80% and scales its icon and label down so every item is on screen, and 8 is the most that keeps a usable cell -- 44dp on a 360dp phone, the one case under the 48dp touch floor), each a ui.sections id, and ui.default_section is one of them. N2 the app compiles libs:bottomnav (a project dependency in its gradle scripts, or build.json modules). N3 no hand-rolled nav widget in the app's sources (forbidden below), comments blanked first so prose about a widget is not the widget. N4 the app's build.gradle bakes UI_BOTTOM_NAV and UI_SECTIONS_B64, and no id literal in Kotlin (id_calls, 'page:<section>/<page>') names a section or page build.json does not declare. N5 a section with two or more pages (or a page with two or more sub-pages) is drawn by PageTabs/PageTabsView or, since #1154, libs:ui-nav-bars's NavBarTopSecondRow (the bar is libs:ui-nav-bars's NavBarBottom; both are N7 call sites). N6 every exemption carries a reason, names a real app, and an exempt app that already passes N1-N5 is stale (it migrated: delete the exemption). N0 libs:bottomnav still ships NavDecl, PageTabs and PageTabsView. N7 (parity, #868 follow-up): the island and the strips look the SAME in every app because the look is libs:bottomnav's alone. In a held app's sources the island/strip call sites (n7.calls) pass none of n7.forbidden_args, no source assigns n7.forbidden_props on an island or strip view (n7.view_hosts), the app declares no resource named like n7.resource_names (an island colour, dimen or type of its own), and some source calls n7.chrome_call (the lib's window chrome). N9 (light pages): every ui.sections[].background and pages[].background is one of `backgrounds` (dark = the default white-glass strip, light = the lib's light strip, theme = the app's own light/dark mode picks one); a held app's code never names TabSurface itself (the surface comes from the declaration, through NavDecl.stripSurface), and an app that declares a non-dark background calls stripSurface( somewhere.

ui_nav_bars._doc: N11 (#1189): ONE shared nav-bars lib holds the first row, the second row (one row, two rows, the vertical side menu with its rail), the bottom nav and the Configs card for the per-section navigation mode. The three per-bar libs it replaced (retired) are gone and no app's build.json names them; the symbols are what the apps and the scroll machine are held to.

nav_ui._doc: N13 THE nav UI setting, declared once for the whole fleet (the owner asked for a Clean nav and a scroll-hide, with the choice under every app's Configs > UI). Modes: classic = the first row (breadcrumb title + AI/Profile/Configs), the second row (sub-page strip) and the labelled bottom nav; clean = a first row that is ONLY the top-left hamburger, NO second row, a compact icons-only bottom nav, and a LEFT drawer holding the page name as a dropdown (row 1, a URL bar), the AI/Profile/Settings icons (row 2) and a dropdown of the child pages (row 3). The first row is transparent in EVERY mode (NavTokens.topRowFill alpha 00). scroll-hide: a downward scroll hides ALL bars until an upward scroll reveals them. The setting is persisted per app (NavUiPrefs, the nav_ui store of the fleet manifest). An app lists `nav_ui` in build.json::ui.configs_ui; the lib draws the card (NavUiConfigCard) as the UI section of Configs > General (the first row's and the Clean drawer's 'Configs > General' entry, FleetConfigsScreen; rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json), or the app draws it in its own Configs. The Kotlin file named here and this block are held equal by the guard; the web shell's generated tokens (cloudy-h-webapps-mob) carry the same sizes.
nav_ui._doc_actions: #1369 an app may declare build.json::ui.nav_ui.actions = "drawer": its launch pages (pages with a non-blank action, every section) leave the strips (NavUiDecl.stripPages) and become the Clean drawer's app_actions row, after the AI/Profile/Settings icons (clean_drawer_rows_with_actions). Default "strip" keeps every other app unchanged.

n7._doc: N7 = nothing app-side can change how the fleet's island and tab strips look. forbidden_args: named arguments at the top level of an island/strip call. forbidden_props: properties that no longer exist on the View hosts and may not come back. resource_names: regex of res/values* names an app may not declare (island colours, dimens, typography). chrome_call: every held app's main code calls it (edge-to-edge, transparent bars: the same window as Cloud SuperApp).

variants._doc: N8 THE declared exceptions to the fleet's island look. An app named here draws the lib's variant (ui.style = its style, the island through the variant's call) instead of BottomNavIsland; nobody else may declare a style other than fleet or reference the variant's symbols, so every other app stays locked to SuperApp's island (N7). No app is a declared exception today: Cloud Search left its search-html variant for the shared nav pattern (#1161). Adding an entry needs the OWNER's explicit request, named in the reason; the variant lives in libs:bottomnav, never in the app.

web._doc: #1158 WEB APPS: a held app whose whole UI is one WebView page (Cordova) cannot call the Compose bars (the Android project is generated at build time, no Compose, and a native host would stack a second window over its editor), so it draws the SAME bars from a declaration instead: its own nav JSON (`nav`: tabs, sub-pages with icons, default_tab, and `bars` = the libs' sizes and colours) next to build.json::ui. The guard (check_web, rules W1-W4 in the script header) holds that declaration to build.json::ui and to the libs' Kotlin constants, so the web bars cannot drift. `parity[key].map` is {nav.json bars key: Kotlin constant name in `object`}; theme_file and bottom_colors_file give the colour tables; sources/markers/forbidden are what W4 reads. Adding an app here needs a reason a reviewer can disagree with (min_reason_chars).

ac_cloud-code.reason: Cordova WebView over the vendored Acode editor (#562, #1158): the Android project is generated at build time without Compose, so the shared bars are drawn in the page from src/cloud/nav.json and held equal to the libs here.

forbidden.why: handles a touch/swipe: the hamburger opens by tap only (no edge-swipe)

duplicate_page_ids._doc: #1199 apps whose build.json::ui still reuses a page id under two parents (N12). Debt, not an exemption: the breadcrumb resolves such an id to its first owner. Each entry names the duplicated ids; fix the app (unique ids, legacy aliases for stored routes) and delete the entry.
